newsitem.title: USA: Sensormatic suspends dividend, takes charge.
newsitem.headline: Sensormatic suspends dividend, takes charge.

text.p: Sensormatic Electronics Corp said on Thursday it will suspend its quarterly dividend and take a $90 million pretax charge in a series of actions to improve profitability.
The company said it expects these actions to result in annual cost savings of $50 million and a more focused, streamlined business.

The majority of the expense reduction is expected to come from the European operations, which have experienced lower revenue growth rates and higher operating expense ratios than its North American and International operations.
The cost reductions will result in the elimination of about 1,200 positions, or 19 percent of the total workforce, and charges of about $90 million pre-tax or $65 million after-tax, Sensormatic said.
Due to accounting rules, the company said it will recognize $48.9 million of this charge in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997 fourth quarter and the remainder in the first quarter of fiscal 1998.
The total cash outlay related to these charges, net of proceeds from the divestment of non-core businesses, is estimated to be $30 million, the company said.
The company said most of the job cuts will be accomplished through personnel reductions in Europe and the sale or disposal of certain non-core businesses in Europe and the U.S.
About of these personnel reductions relate to the divestment of non-core businesses, including the Enterprise Accounts Division in the U.S.
The company earlier this week said it has signed a letter of intent to sell this division to Security Technologies Inc.

Sensormatic also said its board had voted to suspend its quarterly $0.055 a share dividend, adopting a policy of "reinvesting these funds in the company's future in order to build long-term shareholder value."

"The aggressive restructuring actions we are taking are necessary in order to reduce the cost structures in our European Retail and Commercial/Industrial business units and to enable us to focus on expanding our growing base of dealers," said chief executive Robert Vanourek.

Sensormatic on Thursday announced a fiscal fourth quarter net loss of $35.4 million, or a loss of $0.48 a share, including an after-tax restructure and special charge of $34.6 million, or $0.47 per share.
That compared with a profit of $500,000, or a profit of $0.01, in the year ago quarter.
However, Sensormatic said revenues for the fourth quarter ended June 30, 1997 reached $273 million compared with $257.5 million in the year ago quarter.

The growth revenues stemmed from a strong performance in the North American Retail business, where revenues rose 29.3 percent, and its International Retail business, where revenues rose 55.1 percent compared with a year ago.

Operating income, however, was hurt in the fourth quarter by unfavorable manufacturing variances as a result of the timing of purchases, nonrecurring adjustments related primarily to the European operations, and legal expenses associated with outstanding legal and regulatory issues.
Before restructuring and special charges, operating income in the fourth quarter of 1997 was $7.8 million compared with $8.7 million in the year ago quarter.
Excluding special charges, gross margins for the 1997 fourth quarter were 43.8 percent compared with 41.6 percent in the year ago quarter.
